Completing the Bargmann Gaussian integral and a quarter-turn gives positive P=(1-t)^(-1/2) R B_S M_{exp[-t x²/(1-t)]} B_S* R* with same dense quadratic form. T=B*A is closed; its bounded restriction to kernel span has an all-Hilbert-space closure, so T is everywhere bounded and T*T=P. Nonatomic multiplication has purely absolutely continuous spectrum [0,(1-t)^(-1/2)], no eigenvalues, and norm/essential norm (1-t)^(-1/4).
